title: Maximum Number of Groups With Increasing Length
summary: Given an array usageLimits of length n, create groups using numbers from 0 to n-1, with each number i used no more than usageLimits[i] times.
statement: Given an array usageLimits of length n, create groups using numbers from 0 to n-1, with each number i used no more than usageLimits[i] times. Each group must have distinct numbers, and each subsequent group must be longer than the previous one. Determine the maximum number of such groups.
constraints: Create groups whose sizes are strictly increasing.
Each group uses distinct number types, and type i may be used at most usageLimits[i] times across groups.
Return the maximum number of groups.
hints: Sort usage limits and accumulate available uses.
After g groups, total demand is g(g+1)/2.
Whenever accumulated capacity reaches demand for g+1 groups, increment g.
Sorting exposes scarce types first; surplus capacity carries forward and the triangular threshold is both necessary and sufficient.
editorial: Sorting exposes scarce types first; surplus capacity carries forward and the triangular threshold is both necessary and sufficient.

tests.explanation: The limits support groups of sizes one, two, and three, so the answer is three.
Only two increasing groups can be supplied.
